problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 & 1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 5 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]?
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Identifying the Pivot Columns of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
The row echelon form matrix $R$ is given below. What are its **non**-pivot columns?

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $R$ has $3$ pivots in the $1$st, $2$nd and $4$th columns:

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 7 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the only non-pivot column is the $3$rd columns.
